summary: Chat SSE connection aborts mid-generation when router triggers model-fallback
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE streaming chat responses consistently abort partway through long generations when the routing layer performs a mid-request model fallback. Impact: Customer experiences truncated replies and silent disconnects during long streaming responses, causing degraded UX and user retries. Environment: Production (us-west), customer on enterprise tier with model pin to openchat-13b-v2 but routing policy allows fallback to quantized variant under load. Observed: SSE connection receives partial tokens, then a 0-length chunk or connection close; on reconnect the resumed response either duplicates tokens or returns a short fallback completion. Expected: Continuous SSE stream until model completes generation (or graceful failure event).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a streaming chat request to redwood API with model=openchat-13b-v2 and long max_tokens (>=1024)
2) From a client in us-west, initiate a streaming (SSE) chat and ensure network stays connected
3) Simulate load spike or reduce available capacity on the dedicated pool to trigger smart-routing fallback (or toggle canary policy)
4) Observe SSE stream: tokens stream for ~1-3s, then stream halts and connection closes without final event
5) Reconnect; resumed response shows duplicate tokens or short fallback completion

investigation_notes: Support reproduction confirmed with NovaHealth under synthetic load: router fallback coincides with SSE disconnects in ~85% of runs.
Hypothesis 1: Mid-request routing to a compat model variant restarts execution and evicts KV cache, causing worker to terminate or close upstream connection rather than perform graceful handoff.

Hypothesis 2: Streaming layer lacks a transparent retry/continue mechanism for model-variant swap; when worker is evicted the SSE connection is closed instead of emitting an error event the client can act on.
Telemetry: correlation_ids show same request_id across router handoff; TCP socket closed immediately after worker eviction; no graceful error payload sent to client.

Related behaviors: reconnects sometimes return duplicated tokens because new worker replays from prompt start when resume is attempted; quantized variant tends to finish faster but with different tokenization boundaries leading to partial duplication.
Temporary mitigation applied: increased dedicated pool headroom for NovaHealth (raised capacity threshold), pinned routing policy to avoid fallback for large streaming requests

Next steps: engineering to add defensive check to avoid mid-request routing when streaming SSE, and ensure serving-runtime performs graceful abort message to client if eviction unavoidable. Also evaluate ability to transfer KV cache or stream state between workers (longer-term).

resolution: Mitigation: temporarily pinned customer's routing policy and increased dedicated pool headroom to avoid fallbacks during long streaming requests. Engineering patch (PR #4789) prevents mid-request fallback for streaming sessions and causes serving-runtime to emit a structured SSE error event before closing connection so clients can retry safely. Plan to monitor NovaHealth for 72 hours; follow-up will assess KV-transfer feasibility for future seamless handoff.
